evidence: The surface morphology of as-deposited films was examined by a field emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM, JSM7401F, JEOL, Japan) and an atomic force microscope (AFM, NANOStation II, Surface Imaging Systems, Germany). The thickness of as-deposited films was measured by ellipsometer (Model L2W15S830, Gaertner, US) and X-ray reflectivity (XRR, Model X’PertPro, PANalytical, the Netherlands). The chemical bonding information of the films was examined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, Model AXIS, KRATOS Analytical, Japan) with Mg Kα radiation (1253.6 eV). The phases of as-deposited films were determined by X-ray diffraction (XRD, D8 Advanced, Bruker AXS, Germany) using Cu Kα radiation (λ=0.154 nm), and the in-plane orientation was examined by X-ray pole figures (Model X’Pert Pro, PANalytical, the Netherlands), which were obtained in the Schulz reflection geometry by scanning the tilt angle of goniometer, ω (chi), in the range 0–85° and the azimuthal angle, f (phi), in the range of 0–360° with a step size of 5°. Hall measurements were performed in the van der Pauw configuration (HMS-3000, ECOPIA, Korea) at room temperature to determine the electrical properties of the SnO2 films. The optical transmittance spectra of the deposited films and substrates were obtained using a UV–vis–NIR spectrometer in the wavelength range 200–800 nm (Perkin-Elmer Lambda-20, USA). The in-plane orientation relationships between films and substrates were further investigated using X-ray pole figures. The XRD patterns of as-deposited films are shown in Fig. 3. The R-SnO2 film was also annealed at 1000 °C, but no phase change observed. The GIXRD pattern of as-deposited SnO2 film grown on (111) YSZ is shown in Fig. 4. The electrical resistivity (ρ), Hall mobility (μ), and carrier concentration (n) of as-deposited SnO2 films measured at room temperature are shown in Fig. 8. The optical transmittance spectra of as-deposited SnO2 films on YSZ substrates and bare YSZ substrates as a function of wavelength in the range 200–800 nm are shown in Fig. 9. The plots of (αhν)2 vs. photon energy (E) are shown in Fig. 9(B).
